land.text: the imperial possessions of the western Mediterranean under the praetorian prefect of Africa: 'all imperial possessions in the western Mediterranean'

predecessors.note: The Exarchate is the Eastern Roman Empire's own province (Cliopatria folds Africa into its Eastern Roman and Byzantine rows), so the hand-over is administrative; the infobox's 'Predecessor: Praetorian prefecture of Africa'.

land.text: Carthage and Africa, 'the final end of Roman control and influence over Carthage, and subsequently all of North Africa' (Battle of Carthage page)

successors.note: 698; Ceuta, the last stronghold, goes in 709.

land.text: Sardinia, listed in the infobox as 'Byzantine Sardinia', and (page silent) Corsica and the Balearics

successors.note: Passes to the Byzantine Empire's direct rule in 698; only Sardinia is named on the page.

capitals.name: Carthage
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Carthage'; the exarchate 'was based in Carthage'.

capitals.name: Ceuta (Septem)
capitals.note: The table's last exarch is 'Julian, Count of Ceuta: 698-709 (historicity disputed)'.

rulers.name: Heraclius the Elder
rulers.title: exarch
rulers.note: 'c. 598-610'; his son Heraclius became emperor in 610.

rulers.name: Gregory the Patrician
rulers.title: exarch
rulers.note: The exarchate table says 629-647; the Gregory page says he is 'first attested as Exarch of Africa' in July 645 and was killed at Sufetula in 647.

correction.text: modern Tunisia and eastern Algeria (Ifriqiya), Sardinia, Corsica and the Balearics, Septem (Ceuta) and the Spanish coastal citadels: 'all imperial possessions in the western Mediterranean'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The page gives no area; the shape is my reading of its list of provinces (the page detaches Tripolitania to Egypt, while the Gregory page calls the exarchate 'modern Tunisia, eastern Algeria and western Libya', so Ifriqiya is used, which reaches the Gulf of Sirte). Ifriqiya is 485,000 km2. The Moorish interior held by the Mauri since the 530s is not described in the pages opened and is not subtracted.

correction.text: the same, without the Spanish coastal citadels, whose last outposts the Visigoths took in 624

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The infobox's 'Loss of last Iberian outposts to the Visigoths: 624'. The 647-648 invasion left the exarchate in place after a tribute; the interior base Kairouan founded in 670 and the retreat from Vescera (682/683) are not dated as losses of land on any page, so the shape is not shrunk before 697.

correction.text: Ceuta (Septem), the seat of 'Julian, Count of Ceuta', until the last Byzantine strongholds in the Maghreb fell in 709

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. After Carthage fell (698) the table lists Julian, Count of Ceuta, as exarch to 709 ('historicity disputed'); the conquest page gives 709 for the loss of 'its last remaining strongholds'. A 60 km circle is my reading of 'effectively reduced to the city of Septum'.

region.text: the African provinces, the western Mediterranean islands and the Spanish citadels under one exarch at Carthage

ledger.note: 591: the exarchate is set up at Carthage. Infobox 'Foundation: 591'; the text says the office was created 'sometime between 585 and 590' and 'included all imperial possessions in the western Mediterranean'.

region.text: the Byzantine coastal citadels in Spain, the 'last Iberian outposts' (the province of Spania of the south-east coast; the page gives no list)

ledger.note: 624: the Visigoths take the last Byzantine outposts in Spain. Infobox 'Loss of last Iberian outposts to the Visigoths: 624'.

region.text: southern Tunisia around Sufetula (Sbeitla) and the Exarchate raided by the Arab army

ledger.note: 647: the Arabs invade the exarchate and meet Gregory at Sufetula. 'Battle of Sufetula (647)': Gregory, who had rebelled against Constans in 646, fell in the battle; the Arabs 'sacked Sufetula and raided the Exarchate'.

region.text: the Exarchate, left in imperial hands after the tribute

ledger.note: 648: the Arabs withdraw for a tribute. The inhabitants agreed to 'a humiliating tribute of 2,520,000 dinars' and the army 'returned to Egypt in 648'; Africa 'returned to imperial allegiance' (Gregory page).

region.text: Carthage and the Byzantine coast of Tunisia

ledger.note: 697: Hasan ibn al-Nu'man invades the Byzantine coast. 'In 697, Hassan began his foray into proper Byzantine controlled territory'; Carthage is besieged.

region.text: Carthage and the Byzantine coast of Tunisia

ledger.note: 698: the battle for Carthage ends the fighting. The infobox dates the Battle of Carthage to 698; the conquest page puts the end of the Byzantine presence 'by 698'.

region.text: Carthage and the Byzantine province of Africa, Tunisia and eastern Algeria

ledger.note: 698: Carthage falls and with it Byzantine Africa. 'This would mark the final end of Roman control and influence over Carthage, and subsequently all of North Africa'; Hassan 'destroyed the city after the Byzantines withdrew'. The Exarchate page: 'in 698, Hasan ibn al-Nu'man... crushed Carthage'.

region.text: Sardinia, the 'Byzantine Sardinia' of the infobox

ledger.note: 698: Sardinia stays with Constantinople as 'Byzantine Sardinia'. The infobox lists Byzantine Sardinia among the successors; the page does not date its separation from the exarchate.

region.text: Corsica and the Balearic Islands, page silent

ledger.note: 698: Corsica and the Balearics leave the exarchate. The page lists them among the western Mediterranean possessions but gives neither a date nor a taker; I assume they pass to Constantinople with Sardinia.

region.text: Ceuta (Septem), the last Byzantine stronghold in the Maghreb

ledger.note: 709: Ceuta, the last stronghold, falls. 'concluding in 709, when the Byzantine Empire lost its last remaining strongholds' in the Maghreb; the exarch table ends with 'Julian, Count of Ceuta: 698-709'.

wars.name: Gregory's revolt and the Arab invasion of Ifriqiya (Battle of Sufetula)

zones.text: southern and central Tunisia around Sufetula

wars.outcome: Gregory the Patrician rebelled against Constans II in 646, was defeated and killed at Sufetula in 647; the Arabs sacked Sufetula and raided the exarchate, then left in 648 for a tribute of 2,520,000 dinars, and Africa returned to imperial allegiance.
wars.note: The Exarchate page puts Gregory's declaration of independence in 647 and gives his exarchate as 629-647; the Gregory page puts the rebellion in 646 and his first attestation in July 645. The expedition's own commanders (Abd Allah ibn Sa'd, Amr ibn al-As and Uqba ibn Nafi on the exarchate page) are not reconciled across pages.

wars.name: Uqba ibn Nafi's campaign and the Battle of Vescera
wars.outcome: Uqba founded Kairouan in 670; in 683 (682 on the Exarchate page) he was ambushed 'by the Berber Christian king Kusaila and his Byzantine allies in the Battle of Vescera'. The Arabs 'evacuated Kairouan and withdrew to Barca, though it was recaptured in 688'. No land change is dated on the pages.
wars.note: Kusaila's kingdom is the kingdom-of-altava dossier of this batch.

wars.name: Umayyad conquest of Byzantine Africa
wars.outcome: A new army 'in 694... taking Carthage and ending the Byzantine presence by 698'; Hasan entered the capital 'unopposed in 695/6', a Byzantine fleet under John the Patrician briefly retook it, and the Battle of Carthage in 698 ended it. The last strongholds fell in 709.
wars.note: The conquest page gives 694 for the army, 695/6 for the entry into Carthage and 709 for the last strongholds; the Battle of Carthage page has no 695/6 and starts Hasan's advance into proper Byzantine territory in 697. The ledger uses 697-698.

certainty.note: Provincial and coastal holdings of the exarchate: no page gives a frontier; the Moorish interior and the 530s-540s Mauri wars are not on the pages opened.

notes: Cliopatria has no exarchate row; Africa sits inside the Eastern Roman Empire (534-632) and Byzantine Empire (633-) rows, whose bboxes reach 6 W and (from 656) Libya, and whose Cliopatria years for losing Africa do not match the pages (the byzantine-empire dossier author, eu-05, should drop Africa at 698, Ceuta at 709). Type 'colony' is chosen because the exarchate was ruled from Constantinople and was never a separate state, although Gregory's revolt 646-647 shows it acting as one. Pages disagree: the Exarchate page detaches Tripolitania to Egypt while the Gregory page gives western Libya; Gregory's revolt is 646 (Gregory page) or 647 (Exarchate table); Vescera is 682 (Exarchate) or 683 (Uqba); Hasan's entry to Carthage 695/6 (conquest page) or 697-698 (Battle page); Gregory is exarch 629-647 in the table but first attested July 645. The Corsica and Balearics hand-over in 698 is page-silent (confidence 1). Kusaila (Altava) and the Kahina (Aurès) are the Berber states that sat beside the exarchate; their lands are not subtracted here. Gazetteer: Ifriqiya, Sardinia, Corsica, Balearic Islands, Ceuta, Murcia and Almería resolve; 'Sbeitla' is not entered as a place.
